exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Second Derivative of a Parametric Curve Given the First Derivative

question.text: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x = \dfrac{1}{t^3}, \, y= \dfrac{3}{t}.$ Given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= t^2,$ calculate $\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2}.$
question.explanation:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\color{black}\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right) }{ \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} \right)}. \end{align*}

We're given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= t^2,$ and we can calculate $\dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}$ as follows:

\[ \dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt} = \dfrac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt} \left(\dfrac{1}{t^3}\right) =-\dfrac{3}{t^4} \]

Substituting into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( t^2 \right) }{ \left( -\dfrac{3}{t^4}\right) } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ 2t }{ \left(-\dfrac{3}{t^4}\right) } \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{2}{3}t^5. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Second Derivative of a Parametric Curve Given the First Derivative

question.text: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x = \sin(3t), \, y= -2\cos(3t)-2.$ Given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= 2\tan(3t),$ calculate $\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2}.$
question.explanation:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula \begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\color{black}\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right) }{ \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} \right)}. \end{align*}

We're given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= 2\tan(3t),$ and we can calculate $\dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}$ as follows: \[ \dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt} = \dfrac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt} (\sin(3t)) = 3\cos (3t) \]

Substituting into the formula, we get \begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( 2\tan(3t) \right) }{ 3\cos(3t) } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ 6\sec^2 (3t) }{ 3\cos(3t) } \\[5pt] &= 2\sec^3 (3t). \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Second Derivative of a Parametric Curve Given the First Derivative

question.text: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x = 5\sin t, \, y= -15\cos t.$ Given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= 3\tan t,$ calculate $\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2}.$
question.explanation:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\color{black}\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right) }{ \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} \right)}. \end{align*}

We're given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= 3\tan t,$ and we can calculate $\dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}$ as follows:

\[ \dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt} = \dfrac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt} (5\sin t) = 5\cos t \]

Substituting into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( 3\tan t \right) }{ 5\cos t } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ 3\sec^2 t }{ 5\cos t } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac35\sec^3 t. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Second Derivative of a Parametric Curve Given the First Derivative

question.text: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x = e^t-3, \, y= e^{3t}-e^{t}.$ Given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= 3e^{2t}-1,$ calculate $\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2}.$
question.explanation:
To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\color{black}\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right) }{ \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} \right)}. \end{align*}

We're given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= 3e^{2t}-1,$ and we can calculate $\dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}$ as follows:

\[ \dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt} = \dfrac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt} \left(e^t - 3\right) = e^t \]

Substituting into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( 3e^{2t}-1 \right) }{ e^t } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ 6e^{2t} }{ e^t } \\[5pt] &= 6e^t. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Second Derivative of a Parametric Curve

question.text: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x =-2\cos (4t)-10, \, y= 6\sin (4t)+15.$ Calculate $\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2}.$
question.explanation:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

\[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

\[ x'(t) = 8\sin (4t), \qquad y'(t)=24\cos (4t). \]

Therefore, \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{24\cos (4t)}{8\sin (4t)} = 3\cot (4t). \]

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\color{black}\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right) }{ \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} \right)}. \end{align*}

Substituting into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( 3\cot (4t) \right) }{ 8\sin (4t) } \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{ 12\csc^2 (4t) }{8\sin (4t) } \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{3}{2}\csc^3 (4t). \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Second Derivative of a Parametric Curve

question.text: A curve is defined by the parametric equations $x = \dfrac{t^3}{3}, \, y= t^5+2t^3$ where $t$ is a real number. Calculate $\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2}.$
question.explanation:
To find the first derivative, we will use the formula

\[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{y'(t)}{x'(t)}. \]

Differentiating $x$ and $y,$ we get

\[ x'(t) = t^2, \qquad y'(t)=5t^4+6t^2. \]

Therefore, \[ \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{5t^4+6t^2}{t^2} = 5t^2+6. \]

To compute the second derivative, we can use the formula

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\color{black}\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right) }{ \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} \right)}. \end{align*}

Substituting into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( 5t^2+6\right) }{ t^2 } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ 10t }{ t^2 } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{10}{t}. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Derivative of a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.text: A curve has parametric equations $x = 4\cos(2t)+1, \, y = 4\sin(2t)+3.$ Given that $\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} = -\cot(2t),$ determine $\dfrac{\textrm{d}^2 y}{\textrm{d}x^2}$ at the point where $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4}.$ Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
To compute $\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y }{\textrm d x^2},$ we can use the formula

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\color{black}\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right) }{ \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\right) }. \end{align*}

We're given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= -\cot (2t),$ and we can calculate $\dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}$ as follows: \[ \dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt} = \dfrac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt} (4\cos(2t)+1) = -8\sin(2t) \]

Substituting into the formula, we get

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( -\cot (2t)\right) }{ -8\sin(2t) } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ (2\csc^2 (2t)) }{ -8\sin(2t) } \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{1}{4}\csc^3 (2t). \end{align*}

Finally, we evaluate at $t=\dfrac{\pi}{4},$ and we get

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}^2 y}{\textrm{d}x^2} \, \Bigg|_{t\,=\,\frac{\pi}{4}} = -\dfrac{1}{4}\csc^3 \left(2\cdot \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-\dfrac{1}{4}}. \]

example.title: Calculating the Derivative of a Parametric Curve at a Given Point

question.text: A curve has parametric equations $x = e^{2t}, \, y=e^{6t}.$ Given that $\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} = 3e^{4t},$ calculate $\dfrac{\textrm{d}^2 y}{\textrm{d}x^2}$ at the point where $t = 1.$ Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
To compute $\dfrac{\textrm d^2 y }{\textrm d x^2},$ we can use the formula

\begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left(\color{black}\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}\right) }{ \left(\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\right) }. \end{align*}

We're given that $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}= 3e^{4t},$ and we can calculate $\dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt}$ as follows: \[ \dfrac{\mathrm dx}{\mathrm dt} = \dfrac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt} (e^{2t}) = 2e^{2t} \]

Substituting into the formula, we get \begin{align*} \dfrac{\textrm d^2 y}{\textrm d x^2} &= \dfrac{ \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\left( 3e^{4t}\right) }{ 2e^{2t} } \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ 12e^{4t} }{ 2e^{2t} } \\[5pt] &= 6e^{2t}. \end{align*}

Finally, we evaluate at $t = 1,$ and we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}^2 y}{\textrm{d} x^2} \, \Bigg|_{t\,=\,1} = 6e^{2(1)} = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{6e^{2}}. \]
